representation.declared_label: bf16 (no quantization; the checkpoint's own dtype)

weights._granularity_source: safetensors tensor table - no quantization_config present, so this checkpoint declares no quantizer and the storage dtype IS the scheme

activations._source: checkpoint torch_dtype; the runtime was not asked to override it

kv_cache._source: launch configuration (vLLM --kv-cache-dtype; 'auto' means the model dtype)

calibration._not_collected: no calibration step in this config's provenance (unquantized, or a vendor checkpoint whose calibration set the publisher did not state)

representation.param_count_method: summed from the safetensors tensor table

latency._inter_token_caveat: gaps between successive SSE content deltas, not between tokens. A backend may coalesce several tokens into one delta or split one across two, and the three backends do not agree on it - so an ITL comparison ACROSS frameworks is confounded by chunking, while within one framework it is a clean jitter measurement.

throughput._prefill_caveat: prefill_tok_s is input_tokens / TTFT, so it charges prefill with every fixed per-request cost the server has - scheduling, tokenisation, the first sampling step. At 128 tokens that overhead dominates and the figure understates the kernel; at 8192 it is negligible. Compare prefill rates across prompt LENGTHS with that in mind, and across frameworks only at the same length.

memory.kv_cache_bytes_per_token_formula: 2 x 28 layers x 4 kv_heads x 128 head_dim x 2 bytes = 57344 B/token (KV dtype: auto -> model dtype)
memory.kv_residency_note: the runtime RESERVED 34.4 GiB of KV cache, but the board's available memory fell by only 4.5 GiB in total, of which ~-9.8 GiB is left after the weights. Reserved is address space; resident is what was touched, and this workload never filled the cache. A co-resident perception stack contends with the RESIDENT figure; a second model server starting up contends with the RESERVED one.
memory.max_context_limiting_factor: configuration (the server's own declared context limit, not memory)
memory.attribution_note: unified memory, so none of this is VRAM. peak_device_bytes is MemTotal-MemAvailable at its highest during the session and includes the OS and unreclaimable page cache. peak_attributable_bytes is the drop in MemAvailable from the pre-start baseline - what this config actually took. free_bytes_remaining is MemAvailable at its trough: the least memory a co-resident perception stack would have found free.
